start_command: npm run dev:api & npm run dev
$port_comment: Measured 2026-08-03: the probe polled :3001 while the API printed 'SermonSmith API running on 127.0.0.1:3101'. Cause: services/api/.env (gitignored, developer-local) sets PORT=3101/HOST=127.0.0.1, and nothing re-asserted the manifest against it. A probe port is a GUESS unless EVA also DECIDES the port, so PORT/HOST are now pinned in launch_env — the api's entry is `import 'dotenv/config'`, which never overwrites an already-set process env var, so EVA's value wins over any .env — and readiness_probe.port MUST equal launch_env.PORT (enforced by test/manifests.test.mjs). 3101 (not the repo-documented 3001) is kept because 3001 is contended on this machine: when the family-stewardship-navigator compose stack is up, its server container publishes 127.0.0.1:3001 (owned by com.docker.backend). VITE_API_URL is pinned to match, or the Vite app would call an API port nothing serves.
$prereq_comment: Measured 2026-08-01: `npm run dev:api` dies at import time with PrismaClientConstructorValidationError — 'Invalid value undefined for datasource "db"' — because DATABASE_URL is unset. There is no safe default: Prisma needs a real, migrated Postgres. That is an ENVIRONMENT prerequisite, not an app defect, so the app reports BLOCKED naming DATABASE_URL rather than a critical never-passing journey.

prerequisites.name: DATABASE_URL for a disposable SermonSmith Postgres
prerequisites.remedy: create a throwaway database on the local Postgres, run `npm run db:migrate -w @sermonsmith/api` against it, then set (user scope) EVA_APP_ENV={"sermonsmith":{"DATABASE_URL":"postgresql://USER:PASS@127.0.0.1:5432/sermonsmith_eva"}}

journeys.name: Login page loads and identifies SermonSmith
journeys.$expected_comment: SermonSmith authenticates with httpOnly cookies, so the browser holds NO client-readable session evidence: AuthProvider's boot `api.auth.me()` cannot know it is anonymous without asking, and an anonymous ask can only 401. Unlike GeneMap (which gates on a readable CSRF hint), the only true app-side fixes here are a server-set non-httpOnly session-hint cookie — which would read every ALREADY-signed-in browser as logged out until it re-authenticates — or changing /api/auth/me's contract. Both cost more than the noise, so this is declared, per journey, by the exact endpoint. It can never suppress an assertion failure, and a 401 on any OTHER endpoint still reds the journey.
journeys.user_impact: If the login page does not load, no user can sign in at all.

journeys.name: New user can reach the registration form from login
journeys.user_impact: A prospective user who cannot reach the registration form cannot self-onboard.

journeys.name: Login shows a useful error for an unknown email
journeys.$expected_comment: /api/auth/login's 401 IS this journey's subject: it deliberately signs in with a wrong password and asserts the user is told so. Declaring it is what lets the assertion be the thing that decides.
journeys.user_impact: Without a clear error, a user with a typo'd email or password is stuck with no feedback.
